hook: A partial view of a quantum code leaks exactly 1 minus 2 times the failure rate of decoding on that view.
summary: For any region of a toric code and any Pauli noise, an eavesdropper's best advantage in learning a logical bit equals 1 - 2 P_fail, where P_fail is the failure rate of decoding using only that region. A region missing one column of the code learns nothing, and a strip's threshold matches the Nishimori point of the random-bond Ising model. Tests on two IBM Heron processors (d = 3, 5) use an emulated adversary, not a real attack.
title: How wide must an eavesdropper be? Leakage of a toric-code logical bit to a strip and the Nishimori point
